dimensions.assessment: Affects taxpayers involved in IRS collection due process hearings and tax disputes, along with the IRS and the Tax Court.
dimensions.evidence: in the case of the running of any period of limitations... with respect to the filing of any claim for credit or refund

dimensions.assessment: Provides significant procedural protections by preventing the IRS from applying overpayments to disputed liabilities and expanding judicial review rights.
dimensions.evidence: Tax Court shall have jurisdiction with respect to... any underlying tax liability

dimensions.assessment: The source text does not provide specific estimates of federal revenue changes or spending impacts.
Amends multiple sections of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 regarding refund limitations, overpayment crediting, and Tax Court jurisdiction.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to suspend the period of limitations on filing a claim

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent procedural rules applying to qualifying active and future collection proceedings and petitions.
dimensions.evidence: The amendment made by this section shall apply with respect to petitions filed after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Quantitative estimates of federal revenue effects or the number of taxpayers affected annually are missing.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill adjusts tax collection due process procedures, pauses refund limitations periods during disputes, halts overpayment crediting, and expands Tax Court jurisdiction.
